questions: Which existing methods are closest to each component of the idea (passage-local context-graph supervision, adaptive one-hop repair, lower-hop RL for deeper-hop transfer), and does the closest retrieved work (arxiv:2609.12230) already cover the combined recipe and all four hypotheses (H1-H4) in full?

Does the mechanism already exist under alternative terminology that the initial searches would miss (context-aware/neighbor-aware knowledge graph completion, GraphRAG / KG-RAG subgraph retrieval, path-based neural-symbolic reasoning, self-training / skill-targeted adaptive training / data-repair loops, RLVR-GRPO style RL for reasoning)?

Which baselines and evaluation methodology apply: standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks (WebQSP, ComplexWebQuestions, MetaQA) with open-ended answer EM/F1, or domain-specific KG multiple-choice items as in the closest work, and how do option shuffling, retained/cleaned validation sets, and LLM-judge scoring affect validity?

Is the idea feasible to execute with a ~14B open-weight LLM: is the full pipeline (KG/CG construction, QA generation, SFT, iterative LLM-judged repair, RL, 3-5-hop evaluation) reproducible at available compute and within budget, and is code/data available from the closest work?

What residual novel contribution, if any, remains after the closest work, and what re-scoped question is defensible (e.g., independent component decomposition, matched-token control isolating context from supervision volume, or generalization beyond disease-specific KGs)?

Is the central causal claim - that same-passage context augmentation (not merely added supervision tokens/examples) improves deeper-hop QA - distinguishable from a training-signal-size confounder, and what control arms settle it?
Does RL on lower-hop items add gains beyond repaired SFT alone, and is the reported transfer to 3-5-hop queries robust to seed variance and to the small size of domain-specific evaluation sets?

standard multi-hop KGQA benchmarks WebQSP ComplexWebQuestions MetaQA metrics
